name: PT Atlas Resources Tbk

frontmatter.title: Atlas Resources — permit-bound coal priced for a war premium that must persist
frontmatter.summary: Atlas Resources is a small, high-cost Indonesian thermal-coal producer whose value is bound by four years of exploitation permits and a two-thirds-weight renewal credit. On the full H1 2026 cash capex — property, plant and equipment plus capitalised production stripping — the life DCF values the equity at Rp146 a share. At Rp500 the shares price the war premium to persist. We rate the shares SELL, target Rp306.
thesis: The shares are priced above a permit-window life DCF that already carries a two-thirds weight on IUP renewal. The reverse DCF solves to a benchmark of 134.9 US$/t, about 1.14 times the deck's FY2027E marker and close to its war-premium year — the market is paying for the premium to persist, not for a stranded asset and not for a multi-decade mine life [S3][S2].

The permit, not the reserve, is the asset boundary — the Q2 2026 accounts put the last exploitation-IUP at 7 January 2030 and the exploration licences unrenewed. The base charges the full cash capex, so the value-maximising DCF stops well before the permit date, and carries the extension as a probability-weighted bridge [S3][F29][F30][F51].

At the coal deck's through-cycle Newcastle path the effective realisation is 44.5% of the benchmark, so operating EBITDA falls from US$89.9m in the war-premium year to US$10.8m by the end of the permit window; the equity is highly convex to the benchmark [S2][S3].

The base case is Rp146, the bull Rp1,070 and the bear Rp0. The bull supplies most of the probability-weighted Rp306 target because operating leverage lifts a thin margin, and the bear is floored at limited liability rather than held at the base [S3].

FY2025 was not an operating profit — the operating business lost money at the EBIT line, and reported net profit came from a 23.1 US$m miscellaneous line and a low tax base; H1 2026 is genuinely better, but it is cycle position rather than durable value [S2][S3].

Governance and structure travel with the story — a serial issuer (a placement in 2023 and another planned for 2026), a negative retained-earnings balance, no dividend, and a request to pledge assets for a larger credit line. These are disclosed, not disqualifying, but they cap what a minority holder should pay for the option [S2][S4].

catalysts.event: Extraordinary shareholders' meeting on the planned private placement and the asset pledge for a larger Bank Mandiri facility
Expiry of the ALH exploitation IUP, one of three short-dated permits in the group
Expiry of the HEB Baturaja exploitation IUP, which carries the bulk of the reserve base
FY2026 audited results, the first full-year test of the higher-price operating run-rate

blocks.text: **Rating and target.** We rate Atlas Resources SELL with a twelve-month target of Rp306, -38.8% against the Rp500 close — the same direction as initiation, at a wider discount than the first revision. The target is the probability-weighted value after the house liquidity discount of 10.0%, not a price forecast for the next print; the base case, which is the most likely single path, is Rp146, the bull Rp1,070 and the bear Rp0. This revision corrects the capex basis the QC auditor blocked: capex is now the full H1 2026 cash outflow — property and equipment plus the mining-property line, most of which is capitalised production stripping — not the PPE line alone. Renewal stays credited in the base. The life DCF is positive but far below the price, so the equity is expensive rather than worthless [S2][S3].

**The variant view.** The company is not being asked to prove that it can mine coal — it has done so for years, it has a large reserve and resource base, and its integrated hauling and port chain is a real asset [S2]. The question is what a buyer is paying for. The Q2 2026 accounts set out, concession by concession, when each exploitation permit expires, and the answer is soon: the latest permits run to 2030, the main reserve permit ends in January 2030, and one producing permit ends in December 2026 [S3]. A reserve is only an asset for as long as the licence allows it to be mined. The record contains no granted extension beyond 2030, but a producing IUP with three years left is in the normal pre-extension state, so we do not assume lapse: the base carries a two-thirds weight on renewal — a judgement, supported by the mechanism of the long-term PLN supply contract, PLNBBI's shareholding and the HEB reserve rather than by a sourced probability [S2][S3][F48][F49][F30]. One of those three anchors, PLNBBI, is the subject of a Kejati DKI review of the 2018 investment cooperation, disclosed in the governance section and flagged under risks [F60][S13]. What the market is paying is not a multi-decade mine life; the reverse DCF puts the implied benchmark at 134.9 US$/t, about 1.14 times the deck's FY2027E marker and close to the war-premium year, plus the renewal we already carry. Our difference with the price is that the deck's mean-reverting path is the more likely one: the shares require the premium to persist [S3][S6].

**What moves the value.** Three drivers, in order. First, the permit: a granted extension lifts the renewal weight from the two-thirds we carry toward certainty; it is the largest single swing and the valuation table prints the extension credit separately so a reader can see the value with and without it [S3]. Second, the coal price: the effective realisation is 44.5% of Newcastle, so a benchmark near the deck's long-run marker leaves only a few dollars a tonne of margin, while the war-premium years lift operating EBITDA to US$89.9m; the sensitivity table shows the equity is far more sensitive to the benchmark than to volume or the rupiah [S2][S3]. Third, the capital structure: net debt is US$67.1m against an equity book of US$73.5m at the FY2025 year-end, and the planned placement plus asset pledge change both the share count and the lender relationship [S2][S4].

**Why not a cautious call.** We have not stacked haircuts. Volume holds the reported FY2025 level, the strip ratio holds the FY2025 actual, unit costs hold the last actual in nominal terms — a small real decline, disclosed rather than explained away — the royalty is the rate the audited accounts show being paid, and the tax rate is the latest half-year run-rate [S2][S3]. The base carries the renewal credit and takes capex from the best available actual, the full H1 2026 cash statement, rather than from an estimate. The bear and bull shock the same three drivers by mirrored amounts; the bear is set out in full and moves the value to the limited-liability floor [S3].

Atlas Resources is an Indonesian thermal-coal producer with integrated logistics, listed on the IDX since 2011 and headquartered in Jakarta [S2][S5]. It operates through six hubs — Mutara, Kubar, Kukar, Oku, Berau and Papua — with concessions spread across South Sumatra and East Kalimantan, and it produces a range of low- to high-calorific thermal coal together with metallurgical coal for power, cement and steel customers [S5][S8]. The product mix matters for valuation: low-calorific steam coal from Oku serves domestic power and export customers, while the Kubar hub produces higher-calorific thermal and metallurgical coal [S5][S9].

The revenue mix is domestic-led and coal-dominated. Of FY2025 external revenue, coal exports were 96.4 US$m and domestic coal sales 240.6 US$m, with the other segment — largely trading, logistics and services — contributing 26.7 US$m [S2]. In other words, the domestic market is the majority of coal revenue, a mix reinforced by a long-term supply relationship with PLN through the Hanson Energy subsidiary, described by the company as a twenty-year contract for western Indonesia [S2]. Export customers are spread across Japan, China, South Korea and Indonesia, with product quality matched to end-user specifications [S8].

The operating footprint is substantial in area but small in tonnes. The group produced 6.6 Mt in FY2025 and reported sales of 7.5 Mt, the latter including traded and logistics tonnes that exceed mine output [S2]. The strip ratio was 6.6 times and overburden removal 44.5 Mbcm, both reported in the annual operational highlights [S2]. Atlas is a sub-scale producer by Indonesian standards, which limits its pricing power with buyers and its leverage with contractors and makes the integrated-logistics route the more credible path to scale [S2][S9].

The strategy is to move from a collection of mines to an integrated mining group. The annual report frames the business around an integrated logistics chain — mine, hauling road, stockpile, port — and the current capital plan is explicitly about adding hauling and port capacity at the Mutara hub through the MMJ subsidiary [S2][S4]. Management argues that this infrastructure is directly linked to group production and logistics capacity and that it will lower logistics costs and support volume growth [S4]. That is a credible industrial logic, but it is also a claim on capital before the permits that would make the extra capacity useful have been renewed.

Ownership is concentrated but not opaque. PT Calorie Viva Utama and the president director are the controlling holders, an institutional holder sits alongside them and the public holds the rest; the annual report's own register is the cleanest source, and the Yahoo insider figure is not consistent with it, so we use the register [S2][S0]. The controlling shareholders are therefore the Calorie Viva vehicle and the president director; the free float is large enough to trade but small in value, with three-month average daily turnover of about IDR519.1m [S0]. The data pack shows 563 employees, above the headcount in the annual report's profile; the difference is not material to the model [S0][S2].

Indonesian thermal coal is a licence-constrained, China- and India-driven export business with a domestic obligation attached. The house coal deck carries Newcastle 6,000 kcal NAR at 137.0 US$/t for FY2026E, mean-reverting to 118.0 US$/t and a long-run 105.0 US$/t, with spot at 150.3 US$/t. The desk's reasoning is that the current bid carries a war premium plus Chinese supply discipline, and that this normalises as Chinese mines restart and Indonesian output recovers; the press tape since the deck review shows the same bid, with LNG tightness pushing Asian utilities back toward coal while Indian power-plant stocks rebuild [S6][S7]. The gap between spot and the long-run marker is cycle position, not a valuation input. The government reference price HBA is at 126.8 US$/t on a high-calorific basis and the domestic power cap is 70.0 US$/t [S2].

Our macro desk is cautious: it puts the economy in a balance-of-payments-pressure regime, tilts thermal coal to neutral and treats the commodity bloc as one neutral beta. For a dollar-revenue, rupiah-cost producer that is a neutral-to-slightly-negative backdrop: a weaker rupiah helps translated revenue but raises imported equipment and fuel costs, and the domestic power tariff cap limits how much of a coal rally can be passed through [S2][S6].

Regulation is the dominant industry force. Coal royalties for open-pit IUP holders run on a calorie- and HBA-linked band set by Government Regulation 26/2022, with a domestic market obligation and a price cap for power-sector sales [S2]. The royalty is a first charge on revenue, and the company's own effective take was 32.1 US$m in FY2025 [S2]. The DMO cap means that the domestic share of the book cannot earn the export price in a strong market, which is why the bull case is a price-and-execution case rather than a simple re-rating [S2].

Indonesian coal is a licence-bound business: a producer may hold a mining business licence for
exploration or production, and the production licence has a fixed term that must be extended before
it lapses. Because the state owns the mineral resource, the licence is the real asset boundary, not
the geological reserve statement. Producers can hold large declared reserves and still have only a
short economic life if the production licence is close to expiry. Domestic sales to the power
sector are subject to a regulated ceiling, while export sales are priced off the seaborne marker,
so the same tonne can earn very different margins depending on where it is sold. The practical
consequence for a small producer is that licence renewal, not exploration success, is the event
that extends value.

Competitive positioning is weak on cost and strong on integration. The FY2025 cost of revenue was 337.4 US$m against revenue of 363.7 US$m, a gross margin of about 7.2%, and operating expenses were 34.5 US$m [S2]. The company does not publish a cost-curve quartile, but a gross margin in the single digits after royalty and logistics is consistent with a second- or third-quartile position rather than a first-quartile one; a first-quartile producer would not need the misc line to report a profit [S2][S3]. The integrated hauling road and port at Mutara are a genuine moat against local peers because they lower logistics cost and control delivery, but they do not make the coal itself cheaper to mine [S2][S4].

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is high: mining contractors, fuel and equipment are a large share of cash cost and are priced in dollars, so the company is a price-taker on inputs [S2]. Buyer power is high: PLN and a handful of Asian utilities can switch tonnes, and the domestic cap limits pricing [S2]. Rivalry is high: Indonesian coal is a fragmented export supply base with a persistent supply-discipline problem [S6]. Substitutes are a long-run threat from energy transition, not a near-term one [S2]. New entrants are limited by permits and capital, which is the one supportive force — but it also means the incumbents' own value is licence-bound [S3].

The deck's external influences are the war premium in the seaborne marker, Chinese and Indian import demand, Indonesian RKAB supply discipline and the rupiah [S6][S7]. For Atlas specifically the most important external influence is none of those in the near term: it is the administrative calendar of its own permits [S3].

**History.** Atlas has grown revenue from US$246.0m in FY2022 to US$363.7m in FY2025, but the growth has not reached the equity. Cost of revenue was 337.4 US$m against revenue of 363.7 US$m in FY2025, operating expenses were 34.5 US$m, and reported net profit was 2.4 US$m [S2]. The operating result was negative before the miscellaneous line: our EBIT is US$-7.7m and our operating EBITDA — EBIT plus the full 33.7 US$m depreciation and amortisation charge — is US$26.0m [S2]. The company's own EBITDA headline adds back finance costs and D&A to a pre-tax profit that already includes 23.1 US$m of miscellaneous income; it is a different measure, and it capitalises a non-operating line that a buyer should not [S2].

**Revenue build.** The model prices sales volume at 7.5 Mt, the FY2025 reported level, against the Newcastle marker multiplied by a realisation of 44.5% [S2][S3]. The effective realisation is low because total revenue is divided by total reported sales, which include a large block of traded and logistics volume earning only a few dollars a tonne; the coal segment's own ASPs were 63.4 US$/t domestic and 79.9 US$/t export, and the segment revenue and tonnage reconcile to those prices [S2]. Revenue therefore rises to US$459.7m in the war-premium year, falls to US$396.0m as the marker mean-reverts, and ends the window at US$352.3m [S2][S3].

Volume is the FY2025 reported level rather than a company plan, and the July 2026 production halt is reconciled here rather than left out. On 3 July 2026 the company said it had halted production temporarily at several mine areas after the RKAB quota adjustment and the DMO policy, while sales continued from the remaining allocation [F64][F65][S14]; the FY2025 annual report had already flagged the 2026 RKAB adjustment as a risk that could cut production [F68][S2]; and the government's July quota addition was earmarked for PLN's power plants [F66][S16], with a measured relaxation for domestic needs [F67][S17] — the channel through which Hanson Energy supplies the Lampung, Banten, West Sumatra and Pelabuhan Ratu plants under its long-term PLN contracts [F48][S3]. The model's volume line is reported sales, not mine output, and the company said sales continued from the remaining allocation while production was stopped [F2][F64]. No lost-tonnage figure is disclosed and the halt falls entirely after the 30 June close, so the at-risk exposure is the second half alone; H1 2026 revenue of 237.4 US$m already covers more than half the model's FY2026E revenue. The base therefore holds the last actual and carries the volume risk in the bear rather than booking an unsourced decline [S3][S14].

**Costs and margins.** Unit cash cost is 38.4 US$/t, built from the FY2025 mining cost per bcm of 2.4 US$, the 6.6 times strip ratio, and the residual processing, logistics and rent cost of 20.6 US$/t, with the deck's brent path adding a fuel term [S2][S3]. The royalty is 8.8% of revenue, the rate the audited accounts show being paid, and operating expenses are 8.7% of revenue after removing the depreciation sitting in opex so it is not double-counted [S2]. The consequence is visible in the margin: operating EBITDA falls from US$89.9m in FY2026E to US$10.8m in FY2029E as the price converges on the deck's long-run marker [S3].

**Cash flow, capex and working capital.** Capex is US$30.0m a year — the full H1 2026 cash outflow of property and equipment plus the increase in mining properties, annualised — held flat in nominal terms, a small real decline [S3][F45][F46]. The mining-property line is not a non-cash reserve charge: the mining-properties note splits the half-year additions into capitalised production-phase stripping of 9.2 US$m and mines-in-production additions of 0.5 US$m, and the stripping-cost accounting policy capitalises the stripping whose benefit is future ore access while sending current-period stripping to inventory [S3]. Because that stripping asset is amortised through cost of revenues and added back in the D&A line, the matching cash outflow has to be charged as capex or free cash flow is overstated. At US$30.0m a year the forecast is close to the 33.7 US$m depreciation charge, which is internally consistent for a sustaining business, and broadly level with the FY2025 PPE purchase of 32.7 US$m, whose mining-property cash spend sat outside it [S2]. The reported history line is not all sustaining PPE either: the FY2025A figure of US$32.7m is the LK's purchase of property and equipment (32.7 US$m), while the FY2024A figure of US$52.6m is the same PPE purchase (20.5 US$m) plus 32.1 US$m of exploration, evaluation and mining-property additions, so the pack's capex line is PPE plus reserve-development spend [S2][F57]. Free cash flow to the firm is US$55.2m in FY2026E with the working-capital release from a higher revenue base, thins to US$0.0m in FY2027E as the marker mean-reverts, and turns negative in the last two permit years, at US$-7.0m in FY2028E and US$-13.6m in FY2029E [S3]. On the full cash capex this is not a free-cash-generating business at through-cycle prices, which is why the life DCF below stops at its value-maximising year rather than crediting the tail. Working capital is negative, at -15.9% of revenue, reflecting large supplier and accrual balances; that is a real source of funding in a growing year and a real drain when revenue falls [S2].

**Balance sheet and debt.** FY2025 closed with cash of US$12.9m, debt of US$80.0m and net debt of US$67.1m [S0]. The valuation uses the later 30 June 2026 balance sheet, where the position had improved: cash of 21.4 US$m against a short-term loan of 3.1 US$m, current-portion long-term debt of 26.2 US$m and long-term loans of 46.1 US$m, with owners' equity of 80.4 US$m against US$73.5m at the prior year-end [S3]. Current liabilities still exceed current assets and the current ratio is below one, with large accrued expenses [S3]. The company is not in breach of anything disclosed, but it has limited headroom: the private placement is intended to fund infrastructure without adding to the company's debt burden, while the same meeting will vote on pledging assets for a larger Bank Mandiri facility [S4].

**Capital allocation.** There is no dividend and there cannot be one while retained earnings are in deficit: the FY2024 AGMS resolved not to distribute a dividend for that reason [S2][F40]. The company issued 300.0 million shares in a 2023 private placement and is now seeking approval for up to 375.0 million more, the maximum disclosed percentage of the enlarged capital, to fund the MMJ road and port [S2][S4]. Serial equity issuance at a low share price is a per-share value leak, and it is one structural reason we apply the house liquidity discount to the target [S4].

**Earnings-quality flags.** The accruals screen is not the problem: FY2025 net profit of 2.4 US$m was fully cash-backed by operating cash flow, and the three-year accrual pattern is negative (cash exceeds earnings), which is conservative [S0]. The problem is what the profit is made of: the operating business was loss-making at the EBIT line, at US$-7.7m, and reported net profit came from the miscellaneous line below. First, that line: 23.1 US$m of miscellaneous net income in FY2025, far above parent net profit, and a 4.4 US$m tax charge on 6.8 US$m of pre-tax profit — an effective rate far above the statutory rate [S2]. We treat both as non-recurring and do not carry them forward. Second, receivables grew faster than revenue in FY2025, and operating cash flow fell even as reported profit rose, a cash-conversion divergence that the screen flags [S0]. Third, related-party balances are small — a 1.7 US$m receivable from associate BKL and 3.7 US$m of advances received from it — so related-party gravity is not the issue here [S2]. Fourth, the IDX regime is clean as far as the record shows: no special-monitoring board or notation letters, a free float of 36.4% on the data pack, and an unmodified audit opinion from Mirawati Sensi Idris [S0][S2][S3]. Fifth, the auditor is a mid-tier firm and the accounts are in a negative-retained-earnings position, which warrants a quality discount but is not a manipulation-class finding [S2][F41]. One confirmed manipulation-class flag would kill the name; none is present.

**Method.** A coal producer with a finite, permit-bound life is valued on a through-cycle, life-of-asset discounted cash flow, not on spot earnings or a current-year multiple. We weight the life DCF at 100.0% and show the company's own trading EV/EBITDA and P/BV multiples as unweighted cross-checks only: the red team showed that blending trailing multiples into the target made the DCF inert and left the bear case unable to move. The DCF discounts FCFF at a WACC of 10.1%, built from a risk-free rate of 5.0%, an equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country risk premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.26, giving a cost of equity of 13.5% and a pre-tax cost of debt of 7.0% [S0][S3]. The full build is in the table.

**The life DCF.** The explicit rows run FY2026E to FY2029E, the last full year before the main HEB Baturaja permit expires on 7 January 2030; the reserve is not the constraint, the permit is [S3][F29][F30]. At the full cash capex of 4.0 US$/t the DCF produces a present value of US$27.8m of enterprise value and an equity value of Rp128 a share after the net-debt, minority and associate bridge and the renewal credit described below. The engine's life-end label is FY2027E, not the permit date: on the full H1 2026 cash capex the out-years are cash-negative at the deck's through-cycle prices, the cumulative present value peaks in FY2027E, and the DCF stops there. That is an economic cut, and it is disclosed rather than hidden — a reader should not credit the FY2028E-FY2029E rows with value [S3][F58]. The table prints each year's FCFF, discount factor and present value, including the negative tail.

**Why the first forecast year carries the value.** The FY2026E benchmark of 137.0 US$/t is the coal deck's reviewed forecast, not a spot extrapolation: spot is 150.3 US$/t and the deck already mean-reverts to 118.0 US$/t the following year, so the war-premium year is the desk's most likely first year, not our optimism. It is nonetheless where the base value sits: the cumulative present value peaks in FY2027E, and the FY2026E row supplies the dominant share of the DCF's present value because the later rows are cash-negative on the full cash capex. A reader who wants the deck's long-run marker as year one should read the low end of the benchmark axis in the sensitivity grid, where the base target falls toward the bear. That is the correct frame for a through-cycle NAV, and it is why we do not capitalise the premium year [S3].

**Renewal.** A producing IUP with three years left is in the normal pre-extension state, not evidence of stranding. The base therefore does not assume lapse, but the credit is an assessed option, not a model difference. The record establishes the mechanism — the twenty-year PLN supply contract through Hanson Energy (F48), PLNBBI's stake since 2018 (F49) and the 194.8 Mt HEB reserve under a permit running to 7 January 2030 (F30) — and the valuation bridge carries that option at a two-thirds weight; the weight is our judgement, not a sourced probability, and no document says the extension will be granted. The engine cannot produce the figure: the value-maximising life ends where cumulative present value peaks, and the out-years are cash-negative at the deck's through-cycle marker, at US$-7.0m in FY2028E and US$-13.6m in FY2029E, so a run of the same model to the end of the offtake life would subtract value rather than add it. The credit is therefore written into the bridge as an assessed worth and the table prints the weighted line. At zero renewal the permit-window equity before the credit is negative — the enterprise value of US$27.8m less the net-debt, minority and associate bridge — and floors at zero; at half renewal the base adds half the credit, at full renewal all of it. Because the credit exceeds the permit-window enterprise value, it is the single largest swing in the target, and a reader should re-price it rather than take it as model-derived [S2][S3][F48][F49][F30]. The bridge carries the extension value in every scenario, so the bull is a pure price-and-execution case.

**Cross-checks.** The company's own trading multiples sit materially above the DCF because a multiple capitalises a continuing asset, while the DCF stops at its value-maximising year once the full cash capex is charged. The shares trade at 6.9x trailing EV/EBITDA and 1.4x book [S0]. These are trading multiples, not a peer-derived cross-check: the engine prints no peer-multiple leg now that the target is the life DCF alone, so the reader should read them as context on what the market capitalises, not as a valuation. We do not blend them into the target: the commodity-cyclical card forbids valuing a finite-life miner on a current-year multiple, and the red team showed the blend was the de facto method when the DCF returned zero. The dividend-yield method is unavailable: the payout is zero and the retained-earnings deficit prevents one [S2][F40].

**What the price implies.** At Rp500 the market is above the permit-window DCF. The reverse DCF, solved on the unfloored base model, gives a benchmark of 134.9 US$/t, about 1.14 times the deck's FY2027E marker of 118.0 US$/t, close to its FY2026E war-premium marker of 137.0 US$/t and above the long-run 105.0 US$/t. Because the margin is thin, the equity is highly convex to price: a benchmark held close to the deck's war-premium year, rather than following its mean-reverting path, is enough to lift the value from the DCF's Rp128 to the Rp500 price. That is why we read the gap as the market paying for the war premium to persist plus the renewal credit we already carry, not as a multi-decade mine life. The market is not discounting stranding; it is requiring the premium years to hold. Our call is that the deck's mean-reverting path is the more likely one [S3][S6].

**Sensitivity.** The first grid flexes the benchmark against the rupiah: the benchmark axis dominates, and the rupiah axis is second order. The second grid flexes volume against cost intensity, where the strip ratio matters more than volume. That convexity is why the bear floors at limited liability and the bull carries most of the probability-weighted value; it is a property of a thin-margin, high-fixed-cost producer, not a modelling choice [S3].

**Segment-build reconciliation.** FY2025 domestic coal revenue of 240.6 US$m at an ASP of 63.4 US$/t, export revenue of 96.4 US$m at 79.9 US$/t and other-segment revenue of 26.7 US$m on the traded/logistics tonnes reconcile to total revenue of 363.7 US$m on 7.5 Mt of reported sales and to the 44.5% blended realisation [S2]. We keep Newcastle as the engine's single benchmark because it is the only reviewed series with a FY2025A actual against which the ratio can be calibrated. The deck's HBA series is high-calorific and begins at FY2026E, with no full-year actual, and the ICI series is flagged needs_source; the domestic product is lower-calorific than high-GAR HBA, as the gap between the FY2025 domestic ASP of 63.4 US$/t and the HBA spot of 126.8 US$/t shows. This is the documented exception to the method card's HBA/ICI preference, and it carries a disclosed cost. The HBA path sits below Newcastle through the war-premium years (118.0 versus 137.0 US$/t in FY2026E) and converges to the same 105.0 US$/t by FY2029E, so a segment build — domestic tonnes at the HBA-linked realisation capped at the 70.0 US$/t domestic ceiling, export tonnes at the FY2025 export-to-Newcastle ratio, and the traded/logistics tonnes at their own realised price — gives FY2026E revenue below the model's US$459.7m and a little above it by FY2029E. The model's single ratio spreads the blended FY2025 ASP across the whole book, so it is too high in the war-premium year and too low at the end. The base case is therefore, if anything, optimistic through the year that carries most of the DCF's present value; that bias points the same way as our rating, and a reader who wants the domestic book on HBA can flex the benchmark down in the sensitivity grid. The fixed-price traded tonnes are a smaller source of residual error in high-price years. The DMO cap applies to the 50.4% of reported sales that are domestic tonnes, a tonnage share rather than the domestic revenue share, so the capped tonnage matches what the company actually sells domestically [S2][S3].

**Bridge and post-balance-sheet review.** The only non-operating value item is the probability-weighted IUP extension described above. The Q2 2026 half-year was stronger — revenue 237.4 US$m, cost of revenue 197.5 US$m and pre-tax profit 18.4 US$m — but that is operating performance already inside the forecast, not a one-off receipt [S3]. The planned private placement is not completed, has no issue price and is subject to the November 2026 EGMS, so it is disclosed rather than valued [S4]. The MMJ road and port project has no disclosed project value and is funded by that equity; it is not a base-case bridge item [S4]. The full search since 30 June 2026 is in the assumptions file [S2][S3][S4].

**Downside risks.** The first is permit renewal: if the HEB Baturaja IUP is not extended before its 2030 expiry, the main reserve is stranded; we carry that as a probability-weighted bridge, not a certainty [S3]. The second is the coal price: a return to the deck's long-run marker of 105.0 US$/t compresses the margin to a few dollars a tonne [S6]. The third is the cost base: the 6.6 times strip and dollar-denominated contractor costs are a fixed burden against a falling price [S2]. The fourth is capex: the base now charges the full H1 2026 cash outflow, including 9.2 US$m of capitalised production stripping, and a further step up in stripping or mine development in a wet season is the main downside to the DCF — it is the key monitorable, not an excluded risk [S3][F58]. The fifth is liquidity and dilution: daily turnover is about IDR519.1m, the house applies a 10.0% discount, and a maximum-size placement would dilute per-share value [S0][S4]. Sixth, the GPU IUP dispute: the PTUN granted a third-party suit against the GPU exploitation IUP in February 2025, but the appellate court annulled that ruling in June 2025 and the Supreme Court rejected the cassation in December 2025, so the permit stands; the residual risk is the separate police matter, not the licence [F50][S3]. The exploration licences AE, GGE, CWD and BKA remain unrenewed [F51][S3]; they carry no production and no reserve in the base, so they are a free option that has lapsed rather than a value at risk [S3]. Seventh, the RKAB quota: production was halted temporarily at several areas in July 2026 after the 2026 RKAB adjustment and the DMO policy, and although the government then added quota earmarked for PLN's plants and described a measured relaxation, a renewed tightening would hit the flat-volume base before the bear's volume shock [F64][F65][F66][F67][S14][S16][S17]. Eighth, governance: the Kejati DKI Jakarta probe into the 2018 PLNBBI cooperation is a live overhang on the shareholder relationship that is one anchor of the renewal credit; charges naming the company or a PLNBBI exit would weaken that anchor even though the probe does not void the permits or the offtake contracts [F60][F61][F62][S11][S13].

**Bear case.** The war premium collapses: Newcastle prices twenty per cent below the deck, so the effective realisation leaves only a few dollars a tonne over cash cost; Asian utilities defer, cutting volumes five per cent, and a wet-season or barge outage lifts the unit-cost residual fifteen per cent in the same weak year. The unfloored value is negative — even with the weighted renewal credit, the permit-window enterprise value does not cover net debt and minority interests — so the bear prints at the limited-liability floor of Rp0, not at the base. The mirrored bull shocks the same three drivers by the opposite amounts, but the operating leverage of a thin-margin producer makes the upside convex and the downside floored; we disclose that asymmetry rather than hide it. The bear value now moves off the base — it prints at the limited-liability floor rather than at the base's Rp146 — and doubling the bear probability widens the discount to the price rather than removing it, so the call does not rest on the base weight [S3].

**Base case.** The most likely path: volume holds the FY2025 level, costs hold the last actual in nominal terms, capex holds the full H1 2026 cash run-rate (property and equipment plus capitalised stripping), the price follows the deck's mean-reverting path, the explicit rows run to the permit and the value-maximising DCF stops where the out-years turn cash-negative, and renewal is probability-weighted in the bridge. Volume holds the last actual because H1 2026 was already banked before the July halt and no company plan or quantified loss is in the record; the RKAB halt and the subsequent PLN-priority relaxation are disclosed under financials and carried as a risk rather than as a volume cut [F34][F64][F66][S14][S16]. The base value is Rp146 [S3].

**Bull case.** The war premium persists: the benchmark prices twenty per cent above the deck, the MMJ road lifts throughput, volumes run five per cent above plan and the cost residual eases fifteen per cent on operating leverage. The horizon does not change: the same four permit-bound years are discounted and all three cases carry the renewal credit, so the bull is a pure price-and-execution case and the driver table below is the whole difference. The domestic DMO cap limits the upside on the domestic share. The bull value is Rp1,070 [S3][S4]. Because the bull supplies most of the probability-weighted target, a lower bull weight would cut it materially; a reader who rejects the bull should use the base value, our most likely single path, rather than the weighted target [S3].

**Signposts that would change our view.** A granted extension of the HEB Baturaja IUP would lift the renewal weight toward certainty and require us to re-underwrite the horizon [S3]. A sustained Newcastle print above the level implied by the current price, with realised ASP following it rather than the domestic cap, would lift the base [S6]. A completed private placement at a reasonable price, and a clear path to higher permitted capacity, would improve the bull probability [S4]. Conversely, a failed placement, a lender covenant event, an adverse ruling in the GPU police matter, or an ALH/HEB expiry without renewal would confirm the bear [S3][S4].

Ownership is concentrated in the Calorie Viva Utama vehicle and the president director, with the public holding the rest; the annual report's register is the cleanest source and shows the exact split [S2]. There is no evidence of pledged controlling shares in the record, but the company is seeking shareholder approval to pledge company assets for a larger Bank Mandiri credit facility, which is a creditor claim ahead of equity and should be watched [S4]. Related-party dealings are small in scale: a 1.7 US$m trade receivable from associate BKL and 3.7 US$m of advances received from it, with no related-party revenue line disclosed that would suggest sales are being routed through affiliates [S2].

The board and control structure are conventional for an Indonesian family-controlled mid-cap: a president commissioner, a president director, a vice president director and a director, and the controlling shareholder serves as president director [S2][S0]. The auditor is Mirawati Sensi Idris, which issued an unmodified opinion on the FY2025 accounts; the firm is not a Big Four auditor, which is a quality discount rather than a red flag [S2][F41]. Licence litigation is a governance item as well as a valuation one: the GPU IUP dispute went against the company at first instance in February 2025, was reversed on appeal in June 2025 and survived cassation in December 2025, and a separate Bareskrim police matter continues [S3][F50]. The dividend record is empty: no dividend for FY2024 because of the retained-earnings deficit, and no dividend in the price history [S2][S0][F40]. The company has issued equity twice in three years — a placement in 2023 and a planned one in 2026 — which is a per-share value leak and a governance item for minority holders [S2][S4].

The Kejati DKI Jakarta corruption review is the governance item that travels with the valuation. Prosecutors have been examining the 2018 investment cooperation between PLNBBI and Atlas, in which PLNBBI took stakes in the group's BKL and MMJ subsidiaries, since 2023; the company's then director was questioned that year; and in December 2025 the special-crimes assistant at Kejati DKI said the case would be reopened and re-examined from the start for the potential state loss [F60][F63][S13]. The BPK-RI's 2022 audit recorded an advance of 164 billion rupiah paid without an adequate feasibility study and without certainty of progress, and the prosecutors have said the review is aimed at the potential state loss from the cooperation [F61][F60][S11][S13]. As of the most recent report in the record the case is at the review stage, with no suspects named and no charges filed [F62][S11]. We do not treat the probe as a reason to lower the renewal weight: it concerns a past equity investment, not the validity of the twenty-year PLN supply contracts, the HEB permit or the reserve, and the offtake contracts continue to be performed [F48][F30][S3]. We do flag it. A case that names the company or ends the PLNBBI relationship would remove one of the three anchors for the renewal credit, and it is a governance discount on the equity independent of the permit calendar [S13].

ESG exposure is the coal transition, plus the local environmental and community issues of mining in South Sumatra and East Kalimantan. The company reports mine-water management, hauling-traffic management and product-quality controls, and the annual report is also a sustainability report [S2]. The transition risk is long-run demand, not a near-term regulatory ban; the more immediate ESG risk is licence and community consent, which is the same permit risk that drives the valuation [S2][S3]. We do not apply a separate ESG discount: the permit horizon already captures the transition and consent risk in the cash flows.

The dated catalysts are the November 2026 EGMS on the placement and asset pledge, the December 2026 ALH permit expiry, the January 2030 HEB permit expiry, and the FY2026 audited results [S3][S4][S5]. Between those dates the monthly HBA decree and the Newcastle forward curve are the price markers, and the company's quarterly LK is the operating check [S2][S6].

We monitor six KPIs. First, the permit calendar: any renewal announcement for ALH, HE, GPU, GE, DKB or HEB, and any change in the exploitation-area table [S3]. Second, the strip ratio and overburden volume, because a rising strip is the cleanest early signal that the cost base is deteriorating [S2]. Third, the realised ASP against the HBA and Newcastle markers, which tells us whether the domestic cap or the export mix is binding [S2][S6]. Fourth, operating cash flow against reported profit, because FY2025 showed the two diverging and the misc line is not repeatable [S2]. Fifth, the share count and the lender relationship: placement completion, issue price, dilution and any covenant or pledge disclosure [S4]. Sixth, the RKAB allocation and the Kejati DKI review: a further quota cut, or a resumption of the production halt, tests the flat-volume base, and any move from review to charges in the PLNBBI case tests the renewal anchor [F64][F60][S14][S13]. A re-rating of the whole coal complex without a change in Atlas's own permit or price position is not a reason to change the view; the house method is explicit that complex alpha belongs to names whose own asset can capture it [S6][S7].

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: HELD FLAT at the FY2025 actual of 7.535 Mt (F2). FY2025 production was 6.605 Mt (F3) and reported sales 7.535 Mt; the gap is traded/logistics tonnes booked through the other segment (US$26.712m of external revenue, F10), which is why the sales line exceeds mine output. No company guidance for FY2026 volume is in the archived record and the reserves are not the constraint — the permits are. Flat is therefore the most-likely path, not a decline: the explicit window is only four years and the company is spending on MMJ hauling/port capacity to lift throughput (S4). The 3 July 2026 RKAB/DMO production halt is reconciled here rather than ignored: the company halted production "sementara" at several areas while sales continued from the remaining allocation (F64/F65, S14), the FY2025 annual report had already flagged the 2026 RKAB adjustment as a risk that could cut production (F68, S2 p.98), and the government's July quota addition was earmarked for PLN's power plants (F66, S16) with a measured relaxation for domestic needs (F67, S17) — which is ARII's domestic channel through the 20-year Hanson Energy supply contracts (F48, S3 note 34). The halt falls entirely after the 30 June close and no lost-tonnage figure is disclosed, so a restatement would be an unsourced drift the most-likely card forbids; the at-risk exposure is the second half only, and H1 2026 revenue of US$237.365m (F34) already covers more than half the model's FY2026E revenue. Volume risk stays in the bear (x0.95); the permit-extension upside in the bull.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025 revenue of US$363.677m over 7.535 Mt of sales gives an effective consolidated ASP of about US$48.3/t (F11/F2); the coal deck's FY2025A Newcastle average is US$108.4/t, so the ratio is 0.445 and is held flat across the forecast. The low ratio is not a haircut: it is the arithmetic of total revenue over total reported sales, which includes roughly 2.5 Mt of traded/logistics tonnes that earn only about US$10/t (other-segment revenue US$26.712m, F10) and a domestic-heavy mix (66.2% of revenue, F9) whose own ASP was US$63.40/t versus US$79.90/t export (F6/F7). The RATIO is what is held flat; the ABSOLUTE price still follows the deck's mean-reverting Newcastle path, so the FY2026E war-premium year lifts revenue and the through-cycle years do not carry a spike forever. We do NOT fit the ratio to the FY2026E Newcastle print (137.0), which would carry a trough price into the long run. A reader who believes the coal-segment ASP (about US$67/t on the company's own ASPs, F6/F7/F8/F9) is the right forward realisation should flex the price grid; the difference is disclosed in §3/§4.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: TONNAGE SHARE, NOT REVENUE SHARE (red-team C8 accepted). Domestic coal revenue was US$240.559m at a domestic ASP of US$63.40/t, i.e. about 3.794 Mt; export revenue was US$96.406m at US$79.90/t, about 1.207 Mt (F6/F7/F8/F9). That is 3.794 Mt of domestic tonnes on the 7.535 Mt of reported sales (F2) = 50.4%, or 75.9% of the 5.001 Mt sold by the coal segment (the remainder is traded/logistics tonnes in the other segment). The engine applies the ratio to reported sales, so the correct setting is 0.504. We place those tonnes under the standing US$70/t DMO power cap in the coal deck (d.coal.dmo_cap); capped tonnes earn min(US$70, realised price). In the base the realised price is below the cap, so the cap does not bind; it binds in the bull, which is the point of carrying it.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: HELD FLAT at the FY2025 actual of 6.62x (F4). The four-year record runs 8.37x (FY2023), 8.55x (FY2024) and 6.62x (FY2025), so the direction is improving, not deteriorating; there is no mine plan in the record showing a rising strip. The house card permits strip drift only where the mine plan or the history shows it, never as a default. The bear carries a 15% cost shock through other_cost_unit, not a fabricated strip-ratio creep here.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Backed out of the FY2025 cost-of-revenue note: mining cost of US$106.656m (S2 p.282) over overburden of 44.481 Mbcm (F5) is US$2.40/bcm. The overburden and mining-cost lines are the two directly reported quantities, so this is the cleanest per-bcm anchor. Held flat in real terms; the brent fuel term in the template adds diesel sensitivity on top.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: The residual of FY2025 unit cash cost after the mining term: cost of revenue US$337.366m less royalty US$32.109m less the US$30.758m of D&A inside cost of revenue gives cash cost of US$274.499m, or US$36.43/t on 7.535 Mt (F13/F19/F17/F2); minus 6.62 x US$2.398 = US$15.87/t leaves US$20.56/t for processing (US$83.586m), logistics (US$21.107m), rent (US$15.564m) and other mine-support lines in the same note (S2 p.282). Held flat in real terms. The company's own per-tonne cash cost is not separately disclosed, so the check is the arithmetic above, not the data pack's D&A (which is only the US$2.917m of D&A sitting outside cost of revenue).

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: RESTATED FROM THE LK. The data pack's US$2.917m is only the D&A sitting outside cost of revenue; the consolidated segment note reports total depreciation and amortisation of US$33.675m for FY2025 and US$26.435m for FY2024 (F17/F18, S2 p.302/p.304), i.e. US$4.47/t on 7.535 Mt of sales. The cost-of-revenue note splits the FY2025 charge into amortisation US$20.340m and depreciation US$10.418m (S2 p.282), so the restated total is consistent to the rupee. We hold US$4.47/t flat; a cash cost calibrated off the pack's US$2.917m would overstate the margin by about US$4/t, which is why the cash-cost stack above is struck after the full LK charge.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FULL CASH CAPEX, REBASED TO THE LATEST ACTUAL (red-team C3 and QC Q1 accepted). H1 2026 cash capex is the purchase of property and equipment of US$5.575m (F45) plus the US$9.402m increase in mining properties (F46), i.e. US$14.977m in the half and US$29.954m annualised. The mining- property addition is not a non-cash reserve charge: note 12 splits the US$9.710m of gross H1 2026 additions into US$9.167m of production-phase stripping activity assets and US$0.543m of mines-in-production additions (F58/F59, S3 p.63), and policy 2n capitalises production stripping whose benefit is improved access to future ore while expensing current-period stripping to inventory (S3 p.34-35). The stripping asset is amortised through cost of revenues (US$11.890m in H1 2026, S3 p.63) and is added back in the D&A line, so the matching cash outflow must be charged as capex or FCFF is overstated. Per tonne on the 7.535 Mt sales rate (F2) that is US$3.975/t, versus US$1.48/t on PPE alone: the earlier PPE-only rebase was a partial line and is corrected here. Held flat in nominal terms through the four-year window (a small real decline, disclosed as conservative); the MMJ growth project is excluded (funded by equity, S4).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses were US$34.509m (F15), of which about US$2.917m is the D&A not already inside cost of revenue (the pack's D&A line, consistent with the difference between the US$33.675m segment-note total and the US$30.758m cost-of-revenue charge). The template adds the full D&A back through the da line, so the opex ratio must be struck ex-D&A: US$31.592m / US$363.677m = 8.69%. Held flat. Using the gross US$34.509m would double-count US$2.917m of D&A and understate EBITDA by that amount.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: THE RATE THE LK SHOWS BEING PAID. FY2025 royalty of US$32.109m (F19) on revenue of US$363.677m (F11) is 8.83%; the FY2024 comparative was US$28.583m on US$315.151m = 9.07% (F20/F12). Both sit inside the 5.0%-13.5% open-pit IUP band set by GR 26/2022 (S2 p.300). The rate is applied to total revenue_main because that is the engine's royalty base, matching the ratio's own denominator. The band remains the reference and the bear carries a 25% higher take via the scenario narrative; a reader who believes the forward band should be the rate can read it from the GR 26/2022 schedule.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: ZERO, and sourced: the FY2024 AGMS resolved not to distribute a dividend because the company had a negative retained-earnings balance (F40, S2 p.105), and there is no dividend in the four-year price history. FY2025 net profit of US$2.361m (F22) is far below the accumulated deficit, so no dividend is the most-likely path even in a good price year. Dividend capacity is not the anchor for this name; the anchor is NAV versus the permit life.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: OVERRIDDEN to the FY2025 actual of -15.9% (-US$57.805m / US$363.677m, S0/F11) rather than the engine's three-year average of -29.3%. The average is dragged down by FY2023-FY2024, when payables and accrued mining costs were far larger relative to a smaller revenue base; FY2025 is the last actual and the most likely starting point. Using -29.3% would book a large one-off working-capital release as FY2026 revenue grows, which is not a repeatable cash source. Negative working capital is genuine here (large supplier and accrual balances), so the ratio stays negative but at the observed level.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The forward rate is the H1 2026 actual of 35.6% (tax US$6.563m on PBT US$18.433m, F37/F36), which is also the statutory corporate rate; it replaces the engine's FY2023-FY2025 average, which the clamp cuts to 35% and which is distorted by the FY2025 65% print (tax US$4.417m on PBT US$6.778m, F21). That FY2025 spike came from non-deductible items and a tiny PBT base, not a change in the statutory rate, and is flagged in §3 as an earnings-quality item. A 36% forward rate is marginally more conservative than the 35% clamp and matches the latest half-year.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: OVERRIDDEN to 45% (FY2025 minority profit of US$1.069m on net profit of US$2.361m, S0/F22; H1 2026 minority was about 41% of the US$11.870m net profit implied by PBT US$18.433m less tax US$6.563m, F36/F37). The engine's three-year average of 71% is distorted by FY2023, when minority profit exceeded group net profit; 45% is the last actual and the forward run-rate.

assumptions.basis: ZERO in forecasts: FY2025 misc net income of US$23.148m (6.4x parent net profit, F23) is non-recurring (FX gain, tax income, impairment provision, other) and is not carried forward; the H1 2026 misc line was a US$0.975m loss

assumptions.basis: engine default constant; the MMJ hauling/port project is funded by the planned private placement (S4) and is not charged to the DCF

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to 0.0 for cross-name consistency: the primary life-of-asset DCF carries no terminal value, so no method consumes terminal growth. A positive growth rate applied to a four-year, permit-bound cash flow would create value the licence does not support.

challenges.challenge: The primary method is inert and the target is, in substance, a trailing-multiple valuation. The 75%-weighted life DCF returns exactly zero (unfloored equity -US$87.232m, floored to 0.0), so 100% of the blended v0 of 137.76 comes from the 15% EV/EBITDA leg (631, applying peer median 6.77x to FY2025A EBITDA of 25.979) and the 10% P/BV leg (431, 1.115x book of 80.409). The commodity-cyclical card forbids valuing a cyclical on spot earnings or current-year multiples; because the primary method contributes nothing, that is the de facto method. The packet also labels life_end FY2026E and section 4 says the life "cuts off after FY2026E", while the DCF actually runs four rows to FY2029E - the zero comes from PV of US$26.4m falling below the US$44.6m net-debt/minority/associates bridge, not from the life ending.
challenges.answer: Accepted in full. The multiple legs are no longer weighted: valuation.weights is dcf_life 1.0, ev_ebitda 0.0 and pbv 0.0, so the target is the life DCF alone and the peer multiples are unweighted cross-checks in §4. The DCF is now informative: at the rebased capex it prints enterprise value US$68.9m, equity value US$327.3m and a base target of US$371.7 a share, all above zero, and every forecast row (FY2026E-FY2029E) carries positive FCFF. The engine's life_end label is FY2029E and §4 now says the explicit window runs FY2026E-FY2029E to the 7 January 2030 HEB permit, with the life ending at the permit rather than by an arbitrary cut; the "cuts off after FY2026E" sentence is gone. The reverse DCF in §4 is solved on this unfloored base model, so a reader can bridge from the printed enterprise value through the net-debt/minority/associate bridge to the equity value without a floor in the path. CORRIGENDUM 2026-10-29 (L4): the capex basis quoted in this response is superseded. The US$1.480/t (about US$11.15m a year) PPE-only rebase was replaced after the QC round-1 capex BLOCK by the full H1 2026 cash basis of US$3.975/t, i.e. US$29.954m a year (PPE US$5.575m plus mining properties US$9.402m, annualised; F45/F46/F58). On the final model the life DCF prints a present value of US$27.8m, a DCF equity value of IDR128 a share, a base target of IDR146, a bull of IDR1,070, a bear floored at zero, a weighted target of IDR340 and a final target of IDR306 at the IDR500 price. The US$68.9m enterprise value, US$327.3m equity, US$371.7 base target and IDR1,403.8 bull quoted above are superseded and must not be used.

challenges.challenge: The bear case is a no-op: the engine returns v0 137.7596638721763 for both base and bear, and 156 for both targets. The reason is that the DCF floors at zero and the EV/EBITDA and P/BV legs are struck on FY2025A actuals (EBITDA 25.979, book 80.409) that the bear shocks do not touch. So the "probability-weighted" target of 241 is 0.5 x 156 + 0.25 x 156 + 0.25 x 735, i.e. 25% of the weight sits on a case identical to the base while the other 25% sits on a case 4.7x the base. A distribution in which the downside cannot move and the upside can jump 4.7x is not the mirrored scenario set the method card requires, and the report's claim that the downside is "fully captured by the floor" is an engine clamp, not evidence.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The multiple legs that made the bear inert are removed from the blend (weights dcf_life 1.0, ev_ebitda 0.0, pbv 0.0), so all three cases now run through the same life DCF and the bear moves: the engine returns bear v0 0.0 and target 0.0 against base v0 327.3 and target 371.7 and bull target 1,403.8, with the bear floored at limited liability because its unfloored permit-window enterprise value falls below the net-debt/minority/associate bridge, not because a multiple leg is untouched. §5 now states that the bear prints at the limited-liability floor rather than at the base, and the false claim that doubling the bear probability moves the return "through the SELL threshold" is corrected: doubling the bear weight widens the discount to the price, so the REDUCE call does not rest on the base weight. CORRIGENDUM 2026-10-29 (L4): the case values quoted in this response are superseded by the QC round-1 capex basis. The final model, on the full H1 2026 cash capex of US$3.975/t (US$29.954m, F45/F46/F58), prints base v0 IDR128 and target IDR146, bear v0 and target zero, bull v0 IDR943 and target IDR1,070, weighted IDR340 and final IDR306 — not the US$327.3m equity, US$371.7 base and IDR1,403.8 bull quoted above.

challenges.challenge: Sustaining capex is held at US$4.344/t, or US$32.73m/yr, from the FY2025 actual (F24) although the latest actual is much lower: H1 2026 purchase of property and equipment was US$5.575m against US$22.073m in H1 2025, and total investing outflow was US$9.210m against US$39.386m (S3 p.9). Capex is the single input that drives FCFF negative in FY2027E-FY2029E and pushes the DCF below its net-debt bridge; at an ~US$11-11.5m run-rate the DCF's PV sum rises by roughly US$60m and its equity value goes from -US$18m to about +US$25m, i.e. the central claim that the equity is worthless does not survive.
challenges.answer: Accepted. capex_unit is rebased from US$4.344/t to US$1.480/t, i.e. about US$11.15m a year: the H1 2026 purchase of property and equipment was US$5.575m against US$22.073m in H1 2025, annualised at 2x and spread over the 7.535 Mt sales rate. Nothing in the archived record says capex steps back up; the FY2025 spend is not the better proxy because it included the MMJ build the company now proposes to fund with a private placement, and the Q2 2026 net investing outflow of US$9.210m is net of proceeds, so the raw PPE line is the apples-to-apples sustaining number. Mining-property additions are not added again to capex because they are the reserve-depletion charge already inside the D&A add-back, but they are disclosed in §3 and §5 as the main upside risk to this line. The rebased capex turns the life DCF positive, as §4 now shows. CORRIGENDUM 2026-10-29 (L4): the US$1.480/t (about US$11.15m a year) PPE-only rebase asserted here was superseded by the QC round-1 capex BLOCK. The model now charges US$3.975/t, i.e. US$29.954m a year, the full H1 2026 cash outflow including the mining-property line (F45/F46/F58), and the "mining-property additions are not added again" sentence no longer describes the model. challenges.challenge: The base assigns zero probability to permit renewal, which is the single largest bull driver, even though the record shows PT Hanson Energy's 20-year PLN supply contract for western Indonesia (S2 p.42), PLN's investment arm PLNBBI as a shareholder since 2018 (S2 p.41), HEB holding 194.80 Mt of the 268.43 Mt reserve, and continued capital spend on MMJ hauling/port capacity. challenges.answer: Accepted. Renewal is now probability-weighted in the base rather than assumed impossible: valuation.bridge carries an "IUP extension beyond 2030 (20-year PLN offtake basis)" line of US$66.439m at a 0.65 probability, sourced to the 20-year PLN supply contract for western Indonesia through PT Hanson Energy, the PLNBBI shareholding since 2018 and the 194.80 Mt HEB reserve under a permit running to 7 January 2030. The 0.65 is our judgement that the normal administrative extension is granted, not a grant already in the record. §4 states the NAV both ways: the permit-window DCF enterprise value of US$68.9m with the bridge, and the extension credit as its own printed line, so a reader can see the value with and without renewal. CORRIGENDUM 2026-10-29 (L4): the US$68.9m permit-window enterprise value in this response is superseded by the QC round-1 capex basis. On the final model the permit-window DCF prints US$27.8m of enterprise value and IDR128 a share; the US$66.439m renewal option at 0.65 is an assessed option, not a model difference (§4 now says so), and the base target is IDR146.

challenges.challenge: Realisation is held at 0.445 x Newcastle for the whole book, but 66% of FY2025 revenue was domestic coal at an ASP of US$63.40/t (F6/F9), priced off HBA and capped by the US$70/t DMO ceiling, and the method card says Indonesian coal realisation keys off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle. challenges.answer: Accepted in part, with the divergence now quantified rather than hidden. §4 carries a segment build: domestic tonnes at the HBA/DMO-cap price, export tonnes at the Newcastle ratio and the traded/logistics tonnes at their own realised price, reconciled to the calibrated 0.445 blended ratio; it states that the build gives FY2026E revenue below the model's US$459.7m and a little above it by FY2029E, which is the direction the challenge identified. The engine's single price driver stays Newcastle because the deck's HBA series begins at FY2026E with no full-year FY2025 actual, so fitting the realisation to HBA would calibrate a ratio to a forecast year, which the house card forbids; the deck's HBA and DMO cap are disclosed alongside and the capped share is applied on tonnage.

S3 p.112 records that PTUN Jakarta granted SKB's lawsuit on 13 Feb 2025 against the Regent of Musi Rawas decision granting GPU its IUP Operasi Produksi, that GPU filed an appeal on 26 Feb 2025, and that a related cassation went against the company; S3 p.16 also records that the exploration licences AE, GGE, CWD and BKA have not been renewed. Because the dispute has been resolved in the group's favour, it stays a disclosed risk and is not a bear driver. The exploration licences AE, GGE, CWD and BKA remain unrenewed; they carry no production and no reserve in the base, so they are disclosed as a lapsed free option rather than value at risk.

challenges.challenge: capped_share is set to 0.714 from the domestic share of coal-segment revenue (US$240.559m of US$336.965m, F8/F9) but the engine applies it to the 7.535 Mt of reported sales, which include about 2.53 Mt of traded/logistics tonnes and only about 3.79 Mt of domestic coal. challenges.answer: Accepted. capped_share is reset to 0.504 on tonnage, not the 0.714 revenue share: domestic coal revenue of US$240.559m at a domestic ASP of US$63.40/t is about 3.794 Mt, which is 50.4% of the 7.535 Mt of reported sales, or 75.9% of the 5.001 Mt sold by the coal segment. The assumptions basis sets out the derivation and states that the engine applies the ratio to reported sales, which include the traded/logistics tonnes in the other segment. challenges.answer: Accepted. challenges.section: fund record §3 and §5; fund record inputs.volume and post_bs_review
challenges.challenge: QC round-2 FIX Q3 is open. July 2026 press reports that ARII halted production at several mines after an RKAB quota cut (5 Jul 2026) and that Q1 2026 profit fell. The base holds volume flat at the FY2025 actual of 7.535 Mt for every forecast year, and that flat volume is what generates FY2026E revenue of US$459.7m and EBITDA of US$89.9m in the deck's war-premium year. Neither §5 nor post_bs_review reconciles a post-30-June production halt with the flat-volume base; the FY2026E line is therefore more optimistic than the record on a point that was specifically raised, and the most-likely card requires volume to follow the company's plan or capacity, with any departure sourced.
challenges.answer: Disclosed and quantified rather than restated. §3 now records the 3 July 2026 halt at several areas after the RKAB adjustment and DMO policy, with sales continuing from the remaining allocation (F64/F65, S14); the FY2025 annual report had already flagged the 2026 RKAB cut as a production risk (F68, S2 p.98); the government added quota earmarked for PLN's power plants (F66, S16) and described a measured relaxation for domestic needs (F67, S17), which is ARII's channel through the Hanson Energy contracts with the Lampung, Banten, West Sumatra and Pelabuhan Ratu plants (F48, S3 note 34). The volume effect is quantified as post-30-June only: the engine's volume is reported sales, not mine output, and the company said sales continued from the remaining allocation while production was halted (F64); H1 2026 revenue of US$237.365m (F34) already covers more than half the model's FY2026E revenue, and no lost-tonnage figure is disclosed, so a lower number would be an unsourced drift the most-likely card forbids. Volume holds the last actual (7.535 Mt, F2) and the risk is carried in the bear's volume shock and in §5. The halt post-dates 30 June, so the "resolved before 30 June" limb cannot apply; the disclosure-and-reconciliation limb is used and stated in §3, §5 and the assumptions.

C3 says capex_unit is rebased to US$1.480/t (~US$11.15m a year) and that "mining-property additions are not added again to capex"; after the QC round-1 capex BLOCK the model charges the full H1 2026 cash outflow of US$29.95m (3.975/t, F45/F46) — including the mining-property line the response excludes. The C1, C2, C3 and C4 responses now each carry a CORRIGENDUM 2026-10-29 stating that the US$1.480/t (about US$11.15m a year) PPE-only rebase was superseded by the QC round-1 full-cash basis of US$3.975/t (US$29.954m a year, F45/F46/F58) and that the figures those responses quoted — US$68.9m enterprise value, US$327.3m equity, US$371.7 base target, IDR1,403.8 bull — are superseded by the final model's US$27.8m enterprise value, IDR128 DCF value, IDR146 base target, IDR1,070 bull, zero bear, IDR340 weighted and IDR306 final. missing_bull_case.note: Renewal is assumed impossible in the base even though PT Hanson Energy holds a 20-year PLN supply contract for western Indonesia (S2 p.42), PLN's PLNBBI is a shareholder (S2 p.41) and HEB carries 194.80 Mt of reserve to a permit that runs to 7 Jan 2030: a permit with 3+ years left is the normal pre-extension state, not evidence of stranding. The bull narrative also says the company "wins the IUP extensions that keep the 268 Mt reserve accessible beyond 2030", but the bull shocks are only newc x1.2, volume x1.05 and cost x0.85 with the horizon unchanged at four years, so no extension value is modelled. (1) The four-year horizon treats a producing 20-year IUP as certain to lapse, and the same driver ignores the BM/HE permits the report calls lapsed in 2017/2019 while still mining their tonnes. (2) Sustaining capex is held at US$4.34/t (US$32.73m/yr) when H1 2026 purchase of PPE was US$5.575m against US$22.073m in H1 2025 and total investing outflow US$9.210m against US$39.386m (S3 p.9). (3) Realisation scales a capped domestic book with Newcastle (see C6).

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in the archive: royalty US$32.109m and the full cost-of-revenue stack (S2 p.282), GR 26/2022 5.0%-13.5% band (S2 p.300), domestic/export ASP 63.40/79.90 and volume, strip and overburden (S2 p.16), permit expiry table (S3 p.17), H1 2026 capex (S3 p.9), the 20-year PLN contract (S2 p.42). Failures: deck values (Newcastle 137.0/118.0/105.0, spot 150.3) are cited to press [S6][S7] rather than the coal deck; section 4 says the life "cuts off after FY2026E" although the DCF has four rows to FY2029E; section 1 net debt of US$67.1m (FY2025) is not reconciled to the US$54.1m bridge (30 Jun 2026); model FY2024A capex of 52.58 does not reconcile to F25's US$20.514m.

valuation_method_fit.note: The 75%-weight life DCF returns exactly zero (unfloored -US$87.2m, floored 0.0), so the whole v0 of 137.8 comes from the 15% EV/EBITDA leg (631, on trailing FY2025A EBITDA of 25.98) and the 10% P/BV leg (431). In substance the name is priced on a trailing multiple, which the commodity-cyclical card forbids for exactly this reason; the primary method contributes no information and its zero is the direct artefact of the capex and horizon inputs challenged in C3/C4. life_end is shown as FY2026E while four years run to FY2029E. The reserve/permit tension is disclosed but never probability-weighted, and the MMJ project is left at zero outside a bull narrative.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says the low base "is not a pessimism setting; it is the arithmetic", but the arithmetic is a floored zero DCF diluted by two multiples, and the input producing the zero (capex) is contradicted by the H1 2026 actual. Conversely, section 5 presents bear == base as "downside fully captured by the floor", which is an engine clamp, not evidence; a properly run bear would lower the target. The SELL direction is not one-input heroic and survives a capex correction, but the -49.8% magnitude overstates the evidence, and the unmodelled renewal option is assigned to the 25% bull that supplies 55% of the weighted target.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads d.coal.newc, d.coal.dmo_cap and the brent fuel term, but not the reviewed HBA series (FY2027E 112.0, spot 126.8) even though 66% of revenue is domestic and HBA/cap-priced; the method card says coal realisation keys off HBA/ICI, not Newcastle. capped_share 0.714 is the highest in the COAL comp set (peers 0.0-0.54) because it is taken from the domestic share of revenue but applied to tonnes, so in the bull it caps ~1.6 Mt more than is sold domestically. Royalty 8.83%, tax 35.6%, minority 45%, WACC 10.0% and g=0 read consistently with the deck and peers.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual or company plan without a source: (1) capex US$32.73m/yr against an H1 2026 run-rate near US$11m (S3 p.9) - the single input that makes the DCF zero; (2) zero probability on permit renewal in the base despite the 20-year PLN contract and continued MMJ/mining-property spend; (3) Newcastle scaling of a capped domestic book (understates the trough years); (4) no value for the MMJ road/port outside the bull narrative. Sourced and not challenged: payout 0 (F40), other_nonop 0 (F23), strip flat, volume flat, royalty at the paid rate, tax at the H1 2026 rate. Mirrored-shock asymmetry: the DCF floor makes the bull 4.7x the base while the bear cannot fall below it, so the "mirrored" cases are asymmetric in effect, which the report itself concedes in section 5.

FY2025A EBITDA reproduces to -1.95% (model 25.47 vs actual 25.98) at benchmark 108.4 and volume 7.535, with ASP 48.27, unit cost 36.43 and royalty 8.83%; extreme_call, horizon.reserves, capex.long_run and weights.changed are all justified with citations. signoff.notes: APPROVED. Second sign-off on the same file; I have changed nothing in the model, and L1-L4 are answered on substance rather than in prose. Robustness of the call: even at full renewal (weight 1.0, the whole US$66.4m) equity is about Rp243 before the COE roll-forward, still far below the Rp500 price, so the SELL does not rest on the 0.65 judgement. Two residual judgement items are disclosed and not defects: the US$66.439m quantum has no printed derivation beyond the sourced mechanism (QC N1), and MMJ is at zero with no MMJ sunk-capex figure in the record (QC N2); both are re-priceable by the Director and neither changes the direction.
